answerCheck.derivedAnswer: A. Toss 3 fair coins one after another.
answerCheck.reason: Three successive coin tosses create three binary branching levels and 2³ = 8 outcomes. Each other option has only two stages or outcome components.

flags: A table can also list three-component outcomes. The stated suitability comparison is best understood as referring to a standard two-way outcome table.

routes.label: Compare the number of outcome components

answerCheck.reason: The left wheel has two even and two odd sectors; the right has one even and two odd sectors. Thus P(even sum) = (2 × 1 + 2 × 2)/(4 × 3) = 6/12 = 1/2.
Among the 3 × 3 = 9 outcome pairs, only (1, 5) and (3, 5) give odd products. The other seven give even products, so the probability is 7/9.
Among 36 equally likely ordered outcomes, 6 have the first die equal to 5 and 6 have the second equal to 5. Subtracting the duplicated (5,5) gives 11 favorable outcomes, hence 11/36.
The octahedral die has 6 outcomes not divisible by 3, and the six-sided die has 4. Thus the desired probability is 1-(6/8)(4/6) = 1/2.
There are 4·3=12 equally likely pairs. Spinner A has two odd numbers and spinner B has two odd numbers, giving 2·2=4 odd products. Thus the probability of an even product is (12-4)/12=2/3.

flags: The calculation uses the conventional assumption that the two spins are independent. Equal probabilities on each individual spinner alone would not specify their joint distribution.

There are 36 equally likely ordered pairs. For first-roll values 1 through 6, the favorable counts are 1 through 6, totaling 21. Hence the probability is 21/36 = 7/12.

routes.label: Count ordered pairs in a table

answerCheck.reason: There are 2×4=8 equally likely physical bean pairs. One green pair and two red pairs match, giving 3/8. Equivalently, (1/2)(1/4)+(1/2)(2/4)=3/8.
There are 3×3=9 equally likely ordered pairs. Four pairs have both entries in {1,3}, producing an odd product. Therefore the probability of an even product is 1-4/9=5/9.
Among HH, HT, TH, and TT, only HH qualifies. Equivalently, P(HH) = (1/2)(1/2) = 1/4.
HT and TH are the 2 favorable outcomes among 4 equally likely outcomes, so P = 2/4 = 1/2.
A product is odd only when both dice are odd. Thus P(even product) = 1 − (3/6)² = 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.
The favorable pairs are (1,1), (1,3), (2,2), (3,1), and (3,3), giving five outcomes out of nine.

routes.label: List the nine ordered pairs and count the five even sums

answerCheck.reason: The first wheel has even probability 1/4 and odd probability 3/4. The second has even probability 2/3 and odd probability 1/3. Thus the probability of an even sum is (1/4)(2/3) + (3/4)(1/3) = 5/12.
The first die has four odd and two even faces; the second has two odd and four even faces. Thus the probability is (4·4+2·2)/36=20/36=5/9.
The probabilities of zero, one, and two matches are 9/16, 6/16, and 1/16. The expected return is (-1)(9/16) + 1(6/16) + 2(1/16) = -1/16.

routes.label: Count outcomes in a dice table

answerCheck.reason: There are 9 odd-odd and 9 even-even outcomes, giving 18 even sums out of 36. The remaining 18 sums are odd.

flags: Uses the conventional assumption of independent fair six-sided dice.

answerCheck.reason: The minimum sum of three distinct chips is 1+2+3=6. The qualifying first-two-draw outcomes are (1,2), (2,1), (1,3), and (3,1). There are 5×4=20 equally likely ordered pairs, so the probability is 4/20=1/5.

Each inner sector has area 3π and each outer region has area 9π. The regions labeled 1 have total area 3π+2×9π=21π out of 36π, so P(odd)=7/12 and P(even)=5/12. Under independent throws, the required probability is 2×(7/12)×(5/12)=35/72.
